Wormholes itself are hypothetical in nature. Though there are two types of wormholes, one is a Schwarzchild Wormhole and the other is a Ellis Wormhole. A Schwarzchild Wormhole is a bridge between two universes, but they are one-way black holes with no charge and no rotation. For to travel into one, the Schwarzchild wormhole must have a separate white hole interior region that allows the viewer to see the his universe after crossing the black hole's event horizon. The main problem of traveling through a Schwarzchild wormhole, is that it can collaspe on itself and the traveler will be at the mercy of the black hole after passing through the event horizon, then crushed at the singularity. By luck if it doesn't collaspe you can travel through unharmed, but it's only one-way and you can't go back to your own universe.

Now, Ellis Wormhole, or Morris-Thorne wormhole are the kind you see in science fiction (ex. Interstellar, Stargate) where you can travel in back and forth through space-time. These are perfect wormholes that can be used for travling between universes, time travel, and faster-than-light travel (FTL). These can exsist with exotic matter or none at all. These wormholes have no singularty, event horizon, and can be fully traversable between universes. For these, you don't need a black hole. The solution depends on two parameters: m, which fixes the strength of its gravitational field, and n, which determines the curvature of its spatial cross sections. When m is set equal to 0, the drainhole's gravitational field vanishes. < Ellis Wormhole.
